comment_data.body:
> At this point I was really confused, then I accidentally pressed snippet expand when there was no available snippets and it notified me that the lang type was lang = tsx and lang = jsx instead of typescriptreact and javascriptreact, I ended up changing up the lang_patterns to use tsx and jsx and it finally worked

There is [a documented way](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/581724ebb39f4aa70bdbffb891d57d6141d29035/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L786-L787) to interactively see the value of the current context. It was recently added as a part of `lang_pattern` documentation specifically for this use case.

The way default `lang` is computed is [described in `default_prepare()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/581724ebb39f4aa70bdbffb891d57d6141d29035/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L925-L927): it first uses the name of tree-sitter parser at cursor and falls back to 'filetype'. The reason for this is to make it work inside injected tree-sitter languages, like for example in Python/Lua/etc. code blocks inside markdown files: the filetype is 'markdown', but the actually used language should be more narrow. In theory it is possible to use some filetype associated with tree-sitter parser instead of parser's name, but there are several problems here: 1) one parser name/language can be associated with several filetypes (so picking one will not eliminate confusion and/or actually work for others); and 2) there is still no guarantee that filetype's name will be the one used in snippet collection (as Neovim's filetypes are not always the same as "common" language name).

*If* you want to always use filetype as language in context, you can write own [prepare step](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/581724ebb39f4aa70bdbffb891d57d6141d29035/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L655-L659) which evaluates snippets in custom context. Writing a wrapper around `default_prepare()` that supplies [`opts.context`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/581724ebb39f4aa70bdbffb891d57d6141d29035/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L924-L927) should be enough here. I would not recommend doing that, so there will be no explicit code here, sorry.

All in all, if I correctly understood the question / feature request, everything works as expected here.

title: confusion about lang_pattern for from_lang in mini snippets
